messages.content: What is the most visited market in New York?

function.name: museum_data_get_visit_stats

message.content:
**Answer:** In terms of sheer annual foot‑traffic, **Chelsea Market** is widely regarded as the most visited market in New York City. *Why it tops the list* | Feature | Details | |---------|--------| | **Location** | Inside the former Macy’s flagship store at 75 Fulton St., Lower Manhattan – an iconic spot right next to the World Trade Center complex. | | **Annual Visitors** | Roughly *10–15 million* people visit each year according to industry estimates and tourism reports. That figure dwarfs other well‑known markets such as Union Square Greenmarket (~2–3 million) or the Brooklyn Flea (~1 million). | | **Attractions** | • A wide variety of curated vendors selling everything from artisanal foods and craft goods to designer apparel.
• Built‑in dining options (e.g., Los Tacos No. 1, Shake Shack, Eataly), making it both a shopping destination and a culinary hotspot.
• Frequent pop‑up events, seasonal festivals, and live music performances keep repeat visits high. | | **Accessibility & Hours** | Open daily (except major holidays); easy access via multiple subway lines (A/C/E/F/M/7, R/W, B/D/F/M, L, J/Z, G, Q, N, S, 42nd St.) and several bus routes. | While there are many beloved markets across the five boroughs—such as the Union Square Greenmarket, Smorgasburg (Brooklyn), and the Queens Night Market—the consistent volume of shoppers and tourists makes Chelsea Market stand out as the top‑visited venue in NYC.
